title: Brain tumours and the posterior fossa

steps.tx: Cross-sectional evaluation of high-grade neuroepithelial malignancy highlights specific physiological parameters. **Glioblastoma** IDH-wildtype classically demonstrates a thick, irregular, peripherally ring-enhancing necrotic mass with elevated choline-to-creatine ratio and pronounced lipid-lactate resonance peaks on **MR spectroscopy**, reflecting accelerated cell membrane turnover and anaerobic cellular breakdown.
steps.say: Cross-sectional evaluation of high-grade neuroepithelial malignancy highlights specific physiological parameters. Glioblastoma IDH-wildtype classically demonstrates a thick, irregular, peripherally ring-enhancing necrotic mass with elevated choline-to-creatine ratio and pronounced lipid-lactate resonance peaks on MR spectroscopy, reflecting accelerated cell membrane turnover and anaerobic cellular breakdown.

vis.alt: Axial post-contrast T1-weighted MRI of the brain demonstrating a ring-enhancing glioblastoma with central necrosis and surrounding vasogenic oedema.
vis.caption: Glioblastoma IDH-wildtype: thick irregular ring enhancement and necrotic core (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Frontal lobe hemispheric neoplasms exhibit pathognomonic radiological signs linked to molecular status. **Oligodendroglioma** IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted characteristically arises in the frontal lobe cortical-subcortical white matter and shows coarse intratumoural **calcifications** in up to 90% of cases on CT, accompanied by cortical expansion and mild homogeneous or patchy enhancement.
steps.say: Frontal lobe hemispheric neoplasms exhibit pathognomonic radiological signs linked to molecular status. steps.tx: Paediatric posterior fossa neoplasms demonstrate distinct structural morphology upon presentation. **Pilocytic astrocytoma** typically arises in the cerebellum of children as a cystic lesion with an intensely enhancing **mural nodule**, classically classified as WHO grade 1, exhibiting low mitotic activity and excellent long-term post-surgical curative potential.
steps.say: Paediatric posterior fossa neoplasms present with distinct structural morphology in childhood. Pilocytic astrocytoma typically arises in the cerebellum of children as a cystic lesion with an intensely enhancing mural nodule, classically classified as WHO grade 1, exhibiting low mitotic activity and excellent long-term post-surgical curative potential.

steps.tx: Embryonal posterior fossa malignancies present with dense cellular architecture. **Medulloblastoma** arises from the inferior medullary velum into the **fourth ventricle**, showing hyperdensity on unenhanced CT and marked restricted diffusion on DWI reflecting high cellularity and small round blue cells, with a high propensity for leptomeningeal CSF drop metastases.

vis.alt: Diagram and neuroimaging showing medulloblastoma arising in the fourth ventricle with leptomeningeal CSF drop metastases.
vis.caption: Medulloblastoma: fourth ventricle embryonal tumour and subarachnoid seedling spread (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Intraventricular glial neoplasms demonstrate unique physical deformability along CSF pathways. **Ependymoma** characteristically originates from the floor of the fourth ventricle and plasticity allows extrusion through the **foramina of Luschka** and Magendie into the prepontine cistern, commonly displaying punctate calcification, necrosis, and heterogeneous contrast enhancement.
steps.say: Intraventricular glial neoplasms present with unique physical deformability along fluid spaces. steps.tx: Cerebellopontine angle lesions require accurate anatomical identification. **Vestibular schwannoma** arises from the inferior vestibular nerve within the **internal auditory canal**, widening the porus acusticus and producing an ice-cream cone configuration within the cerebellopontine angle with intense contrast enhancement and occasional microcystic degeneration.

vis.alt: Anatomical illustration showing a vestibular schwannoma occupying the internal auditory canal and cerebellopontine angle.
vis.caption: Vestibular schwannoma: ice-cream cone mass extending from the internal auditory canal (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Extra-axial cranial masses exhibit distinct dural attachments and bony interactions. **Meningioma** displays homogeneous intense contrast enhancement, a broad **dural tail**, and hyperostosis of adjacent calvarial bone, frequently exhibiting elevated perfusion with prolonged MTT and elevated CBV due to absent blood-brain barrier vascular supply from the middle meningeal artery.

vis.alt: Histopathological and imaging features of intracranial meningioma showing psammoma bodies and syncytial whorled pattern.
vis.caption: Meningioma: extra-axial dural attachment, psammoma bodies, and hyperostosis (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Sellar and suprasellar pathology encompasses specific epithelial remnants. **Craniopharyngioma** **adamantinomatous** type follows the 90% rule with 90% cystic component, 90% peripheral rim calcification, and 90% vivid contrast enhancement of the cyst wall and solid nodule, containing machinery oil fluid rich in cholesterol crystals.
steps.say: Sellar and suprasellar masses have distinctive histology originating from Rathke pouch remnants. Craniopharyngioma adamantinomatous type follows the 90 percent rule with 90 percent cystic component, 90 percent peripheral rim calcification, and 90 percent vivid contrast enhancement of the cyst wall and solid nodule, containing machinery oil fluid rich in cholesterol crystals.
